# NATS messaging

Use when designing NATS subjects, request-reply RPCs, or durable JetStream streams and consumers.

## Subject hierarchy and NATS Core
- Structure hierarchical dot-separated subjects cleanly (`orders.us.created.v1`), keeping high-cardinality IDs in safe positions so wildcard subscriptions (`orders.*.created.*`) stay flexible.
- Remember NATS Core is at-most-once fire-and-forget with zero offline persistence; use queue groups (`subscribe(subj, { queue: "workers" })`) for horizontal load balancing across workers.

## JetStream durability
- Use **JetStream Streams** whenever at-least-once delivery or replay is required. Set explicit `MaxMsgs`, `MaxBytes`, or `MaxAge` retention bounds (`LimitsPolicy`, `WorkQueuePolicy`, or `InterestPolicy`) so storage never grows silently without limit.
- Prefer **Pull consumers** with bounded batch sizes over Push consumers for worker fleets so each worker controls concurrency and memory backpressure.
- Match consumer `AckWait` to worst-case processing time and call `msg.working()` for slow tasks before `AckWait` expires and triggers redelivery.

## Reliability and safety
Send `Nats-Msg-Id` deduplication headers on publishes inside JetStream duplicate windows, use `term()` on unrecoverable poison messages, and separate credentials by subject publish/subscribe permissions (`NKey`/JWT).

## Verify
Tests checking queue-group single delivery in Core, JetStream redelivery after `nak()`, deduplication via `Nats-Msg-Id`, and stream retention eviction behavior.
